title: Lovlina Borgohain, Mirabai Chanu and Theja Rio Among Northeast Names on TIME100 Next India 2026 List
summary: Lovlina Borgohain, Mirabai Chanu and Nagaland filmmaker Theja Rio feature in TIME's inaugural TIME100 Next India 2026 list recognising 100 emerging leaders across the country.
body:
NEW DELHI: Athletes Lovlina Borgohain and Mirabai Chanu, along with filmmaker Theja Rio from Nagaland, have been featured in the inaugural TIME100 Next India 2026 list, bringing recognition to emerging talent from Northeast India.

Announced by global media brand TIME on November 19, the first-ever India edition recognises 100 emerging leaders and personalities whose work is contributing to the future of the country across fields such as sports, entertainment, business, science, technology and advocacy.

**Northeast Athletes Recognised**

Olympic medallists Lovlina Borgohain and Mirabai Chanu are among the sportspersons featured in the list.

Lovlina Borgohain, the boxer from Assam, won a bronze medal at the Tokyo 2020 Olympic Games in the women's welterweight category. Mirabai Chanu, from Manipur, won a silver medal in weightlifting at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics in the women's 49kg category.

Their inclusion highlights the contribution of athletes from the Northeast to India's sporting achievements and their continued presence on major national and international platforms.

**Nagaland Filmmaker Theja Rio Also Featured**

Nagaland filmmaker Theja Rio has also been included in the inaugural list. He is known for his debut feature film Angh, which won the Platform Prize at the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF).

Set in the 1960s and rooted in the history and traditions of the Konyak community, the film explores themes of culture, identity, faith and generational change.

Rio's recognition follows the international attention received by Angh, which brought a story rooted in Nagaland to a wider audience. His inclusion also highlights the growing visibility of filmmakers and creative voices from the Northeast.

**TIME Launches First India Edition of TIME100 Next**

According to TIME, the inaugural TIME100 Next India list was selected by its journalists in India and across the world. It features individuals from diverse professional backgrounds who are shaping developments in their respective fields.

The list includes several prominent personalities from entertainment, music, sports, business, science and social advocacy. Among the other names featured are actor Alia Bhatt, filmmaker Aryan Khan, director Payal Kapadia, Skyroot co-founder Pawan Kumar Chandana, singer Diljit Dosanjh and Indian women's cricket captain Harmanpreet Kaur.

TIME is scheduled to publish the special December 7 issue featuring the list. An inaugural TIME100 Next India gala is also planned for December 12 at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai.

The inclusion of Lovlina Borgohain, Mirabai Chanu and Theja Rio places the Northeast among the regions represented in this national recognition of emerging talent and achievement.

Source: India Today NE; TIME's announcement carried by PR Newswire; PTI; The Times of India.
